Rae: Quick sync — I opened a PR to harmonize streaming + pagination snippets across Python/TS/Go: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1280
Ben: Nice. Tests flagged two issues: a missing include (includes/old_py_example.md) and the TS snippet still uses the deprecated helper.
Isha: Let's standardize on client.responses.paginate() + client.responses.stream(cursor). For TS use `for await`, Python show a short sync and an async example, Go expose a small helper that returns a channel.
Rae: Also add a tiny, dependency-free retry helper and a one-line note about idempotency keys for non-idempotent create() calls. Keep everything minimal so snippet-extractor tests stay fast.
ci-bot: Preview build created: https://deploys.redwood.dev/preview/5429 — results: 1 error (include not found: includes/old_py_example.md), 4 warnings.
Rae: Removed the old include and replaced it with two tiny Python examples. Draft Python sync example:
```py
from redwood import Redwood
import time, random

client = Redwood()

def simple_backoff(fn, attempts=3):
    for i in range(attempts):
        try:
            return fn()
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(min(2**i + random.random(), 6))
    raise

for page in client.responses.paginate(model='rw-medium', page_size=2):
    for chunk in client.responses.stream(page.cursor):
        print(getattr(chunk, 'text', '') or getattr(chunk, 'delta', ''))

# safe create with idempotency key
resp = simple_backoff(lambda: client.responses.create(model='rw-medium', input='hello', idempotency_key='op-42'))
print(resp)
```
Isha: TS snippet (for-await-of):
```ts
for await (const page of client.responses.paginate({ model: 'rw-medium', page_size: 2 })) {
  for await (const part of client.responses.stream(page.cursor)) {
    console.log(part.delta ?? part.text)
  }
}
```
Isha: Go main doc will show the helper usage only:
```go
ch := StreamWithPagination(client, "rw-medium", 2)
for chunk := range ch {
    fmt.Println(chunk.Text)
}
```
Rae: Added docs-bot suggestion: one-line caution: "Persist the cursor between pages; re-requesting a completed cursor can re-deliver tokens and may incur duplicate charges." Also noted idempotency for retries.
Ben: I fixed the include path and updated the snippet-verifier to accept both sync/async Python snippets. Left one tiny nit on variable naming.

Rae: Great — merging after I add a short changelog entry to docs/changelog/2026-03.md and a FAQ blurb in docs/migration/2026-streaming.md about long-running streams and cursor persistence.
Isha: Filed a follow-up issue to add an idempotency example in snippet unit tests so we don't regress.
Rae: Thanks all — small, focused change, should reduce confusion for readers. :thumbsup:
